PLAINTIFE’S MOTION UNDER FEDERAL RULE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE
26(d)(1) FOR LEAVE TO SERVE FOUR LIMITED INTERROGATORIES ON
META PLATFORMS, INC. BEFORE THE RULE 26(f) CONFERENCE

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine, pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(d)(1),
moves for leave to serve four interrogatories on Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”) before
the conference required by Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(f). The four interrogatories are set
forth in Exhibit A and are reproduced verbatim here:

INTERROGATORY NO. 1: Between July 1, 2022 and April 22, 2026, did Meta

submit to NCMEC a CyberTipline report in connection with the Facebook account
associated with Plaintiff and terminated on or about July 4, 2022?

INTERROGATORY NO. 2: Did any such report, as submitted by Meta, contain or
otherwise identify “Marvelle J. Ballentine”?

INTERROGATORY NO. 3: Did any such report, as submitted by Meta, contain or
otherwise identify “Jay Ballentine”?

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document54_ Filed 09/03/26 Page 2 of 5 PagelD# 461

INTERROGATORY NO. 4: Did any such report, as submitted by Meta, contain or

otherwise identify jaychizza@icloud.com?

Meta may answer each interrogatory with one of three responses: “Yes,” “No,” or “Unable
to determine after reasonable inquiry.” The interrogatories seek no explanation and no report
content.

Meta has moved to dismiss. ECF No. 21. Its Memorandum in Support (ECF No. 22)
describes the discovery Plaintiff previously sought from Meta as “whether Meta filed a
CyberTipline report regarding Plaintiff's [Facebook] account.” ECF No. 22 at 6. The
Memorandum characterizes NCMEC’s April 22, 2026 letters as “the exact discovery that Hall and
NCMEC provided,” id. at 9, and states that NCMEC “provided him with exactly what he asked
for,” id. at 11. The same Memorandum recites that the letters “did not state that Meta... submitted
either report, that either report concerned Plaintiffs Facebook account, or that either report”
concerned the disablement of that account. Id. at 7 (quoting FAC 4 92). The Memorandum nowhere
states that Meta submitted either report. The four interrogatories ask Meta whether its own records
establish those propositions.

This Motion seeks no other relief. The requested relief consists exclusively of four answers
under Rule 33. The Motion seeks no production of any report or any portion of any report; no
report content, narrative, report number, communication, or metadata; no document request,
deposition, or third-party discovery; no follow-up discovery; no discovery from any Defendant
other than Meta; and no commencement of general discovery. General discovery remains closed.
The grounds for this Motion are set forth in the accompanying Memorandum in Support. A

proposed order and Exhibit A are submitted herewith.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document54_ Filed 09/03/26 Page 3 of 5 PagelD# 462

Pursuant to Local Civil Rule 37(E), Plaintiff and counsel for Meta conferred by telephone
on September 3, 2026 regarding the four interrogatories set forth in Exhibit A. Meta did not agree
to answer the interrogatories. The parties were unable to resolve the discovery matter.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court grant leave under Rule 26(d)
(1) to serve the four interrogatories set forth in Exhibit A on Meta before the Rule 26(f) conference;
require Meta to answer them under oath, pursuant to Rule 33, within seven calendar days after
service, or within such other short period as the Court directs; and grant such other relief as it

deems just.

Date: September 3, 2026 Respectfully submitted,

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE
